## The test in one box

Two papers, **75 minutes each, taken back to back with no break between them** — **20 multiple-choice
questions** per paper, so **3 min 45 s per question**, and **150 minutes in the chair without
stopping**. **No calculator. No formula booklet. No penalty for a wrong answer**, so never leave a
blank. One overall score from **1.0 to 9.0**; a typical candidate scores about **4.5**, and roughly
**10% score above 7.0**.

**Paper 1 — Applications of Mathematical Knowledge.** AS-level pure content, but engineered so the
direct route is too slow. You are being tested on finding the *shorter* route.
**Paper 2 — Mathematical Reasoning.** Logic, proof, and finding the error in a false proof. Assumes
everything in Paper 1 *plus* material no A-Level course teaches.

Full detail: **[The Test](about/format.qmd)** — format, scoring, what changed in 2024, how to prepare.
:::

---

## Specification — the topics each paper can test

Straight from the official *Content Specification (2026–27)*. **Paper 1** draws on **Section 1** (the
mathematics, MM1–MM8, below). **Paper 2** draws on **everything in Section 1** *and* adds **Section 2**
(logic, proof and spotting errors). Nothing outside these lists can be examined — so anything marked
"beyond spec / MAT extension" in a clinic is enrichment, not exam material.

### Paper 1 — Section 1: the mathematics (both papers rely on this)

| Code | Topic | What it covers |
|---|---|---|
| **MM1** | **Algebra & functions** | Laws of indices (all rational exponents) · surds · quadratics, the discriminant & completing the square · simultaneous equations (one linear + one quadratic) · linear & quadratic inequalities · polynomial manipulation (expanding, factorising, the factor theorem, algebraic division) · one-to-one vs many-to-one functions |
| **MM2** | **Sequences & series** | Sequences from an $n$th-term formula or a recurrence · arithmetic series (and $\sum$ of the first $n$ naturals) · sum of a **finite** geometric series · binomial expansion of $(1+x)^n$ and $(a+bx)^n$ for positive integer $n$ |
| **MM3** | **Coordinate geometry** | Straight line: $y-y_1=m(x-x_1)$, $ax+by+c=0$, parallel & perpendicular conditions · circle: $(x-a)^2+(y-b)^2=r^2$ and $x^2+y^2+cx+dy+e=0$ · circle properties: chord ⟂-from-centre, tangent ⟂ radius, angle at centre $=2\times$ circumference, angle in a semicircle, same-segment, cyclic quadrilateral, alternate segment |
| **MM4** | **Trigonometry** | Sine & cosine rules and area $\tfrac12ab\sin C$ · radians, arc length, sector & segment area · exact values at $0°,30°,45°,60°,90°$ · graphs, symmetry & periodicity of $\sin,\cos,\tan$ · identities $\tan\theta=\tfrac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$, $\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta=1$ · solving trig equations in a given interval |
| **MM5** | **Exponentials & logarithms** | $y=a^x$ and its graph (positive $a$) · the laws of logarithms · solving $a^x=b$ and equations reducible to it. *(No $e$, $e^x$ or $\ln x$; change-of-base is not examined.)* |
| **MM6** | **Differentiation** | Derivative as the gradient of the tangent · differentiate $x^n$ for rational $n$ (sums & differences) · applications: gradients, **tangents**, **normals**, **stationary points** (maxima/minima), increasing/decreasing |
| **MM7** | **Integration** | Definite integration as area between a curve and an axis · integrate $x^n$ ($n\neq-1$) · the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus · combining integrals over equal/contiguous ranges · the trapezium rule · solving $\tfrac{dy}{dx}=f(x)$ |
| **MM8** | **Graphs of functions** | Sketch common functions · transformations of $y=f(x)$ (translations, stretches, reflections, compositions, $f(g(x))$) · effect of $m,c$ in $y=mx+c$ and of $a,b,c$ in $y=a(x+b)^2+c$ · use differentiation to fix the shape · where graphs meet the axes / each other · geometric meaning of algebraic solutions |

### Paper 2 — Section 2: reasoning (on top of all of Section 1)

| Code | Strand | What it covers |
|---|---|---|
| **Arg1–4** | **Logic of arguments** | *true / false*, *and / or / not* · the forms *if A then B*, *A if B*, *A only if B*, *A if and only if B* · converse & contrapositive · **necessary and sufficient** · **for all / for some / there exists** · negating any of these |
| **Prf1–5** | **Mathematical proof** | Direct deductive proof · proof by cases · proof by contradiction · disproof by counterexample · deducing implications · conjecturing from small cases then justifying · rearranging statements into a correct proof · sophisticated multi-step reasoning |
| **Err1–2** | **Errors in proofs** | Spotting the flaw in a purported proof · common fallacies, e.g. "$ab=ac\Rightarrow b=c$" or "$\sin A=\sin B\Rightarrow A=B$" |

*(Paper 2 uses no symbolic logic notation, no formal truth tables.)*

::: {.callout-note}
## This archive is complete and closed

2023 was the last paper-based sitting. Since 2024 the TMUA has been computer-based at Pearson VUE and
**no further papers are published**, so these nine sittings — 360 questions — are all there is.
Spend them deliberately: keep the three most recent unseen for timed mocks near the test date, and
treat 2019–2023 as the best model of what the live test now asks.
:::

## Paper 2 Toolkit — Logic and Proof

The part that is **not in the A-Level syllabus**. A student can be excellent at A-Level Maths and still
score badly on Paper 2, simply because nobody ever told them what *"A only if B"* means. Work through
these in order — each is built on the one before.

| | Session | Class material | Assignment | Spec |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **S1** | **Statement forms — if, only if, if and only if** | **[Concepts](toolkit/s01_concepts.qmd)** · **[Material](toolkit/s01_statement_forms.qmd)** | **[Questions](toolkit/s01_assignment_student.qmd)** · [MS](toolkit/s01_assignment_ms.qmd) | Arg1 |
| **S2** | **Converse and contrapositive** | **[Concepts](toolkit/s02_concepts.qmd)** · **[Material](toolkit/s02_converse_contrapositive.qmd)** | **[Questions](toolkit/s02_assignment_student.qmd)** · [MS](toolkit/s02_assignment_ms.qmd) | Arg1 |
| **S3** | **Necessary and sufficient** | **[Concepts](toolkit/s03_concepts.qmd)** · **[Material](toolkit/s03_necessary_sufficient.qmd)** | **[Questions](toolkit/s03_assignment_student.qmd)** · [MS](toolkit/s03_assignment_ms.qmd) | Arg2 |
| **S4** | **Quantifiers and negation** | **[Concepts](toolkit/s04_concepts.qmd)** · **[Material](toolkit/s04_quantifiers_negation.qmd)** | **[Questions](toolkit/s04_assignment_student.qmd)** · [MS](toolkit/s04_assignment_ms.qmd) | Arg3, Arg4 |
| **S5** | **Proof methods** — direct, cases, contradiction, counterexample | **[Concepts](toolkit/s05_concepts.qmd)** · **[Material](toolkit/s05_proof_methods.qmd)** | **[Questions](toolkit/s05_assignment_student.qmd)** · [MS](toolkit/s05_assignment_ms.qmd) | Prf1 |
| **S6** | **Scrambled proofs** — order a jumbled proof fast | **[Concepts](toolkit/s06_concepts.qmd)** · **[Material](toolkit/s06_scrambled_proofs.qmd)** | **[Questions](toolkit/s06_assignment_student.qmd)** · [MS](toolkit/s06_assignment_ms.qmd) · **[Extra practice](toolkit/s06_extra_practice.qmd)** | Prf4 |
| **S7** | **Spot the error** — find the flaw in a convincing proof | **[Concepts](toolkit/s07_concepts.qmd)** · **[Material](toolkit/s07_spot_the_error.qmd)** | **[Questions](toolkit/s07_assignment_student.qmd)** · [MS](toolkit/s07_assignment_ms.qmd) | Err1, Err2 |
| **Quiz** | **Concepts Quiz — Sessions 1–7** — recall questions + a consolidated True/False memory bank | **[Open the quiz](toolkit/paper2_quiz.qmd)** | — | S1–S7 |

*(All seven toolkit sessions written. Toolkit overview: **[Paper 2 Toolkit](toolkit/index.qmd)**.)*
